findings.summary: The test 'refreshes once when an event is newer, or the snapshot is 15 minutes old' does not prove an event triggers a refresh. It asserts toBeLessThanOrEqual(1) list calls. It also builds a wake time of t0 - 1, which is before the stored fetchedAt, so the age check passes whatever the event does. The future variable and the receivedAt future timestamp are never used. Only the 15-minute branch is asserted tightly. Please add a deterministic case: write an event file whose mtime is newer than fetchedAt, then assert exactly one list call.

findings.summary: Race: fetchedAt is stamped after the gh pr list call returns. A webhook event recorded while the list call was in flight has an mtime at or before fetchedAt. quietSince then treats it as already seen, so the snapshot can be reused for up to 15 minutes without the newer state. This is bounded by the 15-minute refresh, so it costs latency only. Stamping fetchedAt before issuing the call would close the window.

findings.summary: The snapshot runner silently drops any field a consumer requests that is not in SNAPSHOT_FIELDS, because Object.fromEntries yields undefined and JSON.stringify omits it. The current four consumers' fields are all covered, so there is no bug today. A guard that falls through to the real run when a requested field is not in the snapshot would be safer.
